name: TPS54340DDAR
title: Buck converter, 4.5 V to 42 V in, 3.5 A, pulse-skipping Eco-mode
summary: TPS54340 is a non-synchronous buck regulator with a 92 mΩ high-side MOSFET, running from 4.5 V to 42 V (45 V absolute) and delivering 3.5 A continuous with an external catch diode. It uses peak current mode control at a fixed 100 kHz to 2.5 MHz, set by a resistor or locked to an external clock. Light loads are handled by pulse skipping (146 µA quiescent), and shutdown draws about 1 µA. It has an adjustable UVLO on EN, internal soft-start, cycle-by-cycle current limit with frequency foldback, overvoltage and thermal protection, in an 8-pin HSOP PowerPAD package.
key_figures: 4.5 V to 42 V (45 V abs max)
100 kHz to 2500 kHz; sync 160 kHz to 2300 kHz

notes: An automotive-qualified (AEC-Q100) version is sold as TPS54340-Q1.
TPS54340DDA: HSOP (8), body 4.89 mm × 3.9 mm.

pins.name: BOOT
pins.function: Gate-drive supply for the high-side switch. Needs a capacitor to SW; when that capacitor's voltage drops too low to drive the MOSFET, switching stops until it is recharged.

pins.name: VIN
pins.function: Supply input, 4.5 V to 42 V in operation.

pins.name: EN
pins.function: Enable. An internal current source pulls it up, so an open pin runs the part; below 1.2 V the part is off. A two-resistor divider from VIN sets a higher input undervoltage lockout and its hysteresis.

pins.name: RT/CLK
pins.function: Frequency set. With a resistor to ground, an internal amplifier holds the pin at a fixed voltage and the resistor sets the switching frequency. Driven above the PLL upper threshold, it turns into a high-impedance input that clocks the PLL; if the clock edges stop, resistor mode returns.

pins.name: FB
pins.function: Inverting input of the gm error amplifier; the output divider connects to it.

pins.name: COMP
pins.function: Error amplifier output, which also feeds the PWM current comparator. The frequency compensation network goes from this pin to ground.

pins.name: SW
pins.function: Switch node, driven by the source terminal of the integrated high-side MOSFET.

pins.name: PAD
pins.function: Exposed thermal pad. Solder it to the board and connect it to GND for correct operation.

circuits.title: 3.3 V, 3.5 A buck converter, 6 V to 42 V input
circuits.description: A 600 kHz step-down converter that turns 6 V to 42 V into 3.3 V at up to 3.5 A. C1 and C2 (2.2 µF, 100 V ceramics) bypass the input. R1 and R2 divide VIN onto EN so that switching starts at about 5.75 V and stops at about 4.5 V. R3 sets the frequency. C4 is the boot capacitor from BOOT to SW. D1, a 5 A Schottky, is the catch diode from ground to SW, and L1 with C6 filters the output. R5 and R6 feed 3.3 V back to FB against the 0.8 V reference. R4 and C5 form the compensation zero on COMP and C8 adds a high-frequency pole.

parts.note: B560C-13-F, 60 V 5 A Schottky catch diode

notes: At 12 V in, the converter goes into discontinuous conduction below about 342 mA and into Eco-mode below about 31.4 mA; with no load it draws 237 µA from the input.
The parts fit in an estimated 1.025 in² (661 mm²) of board, not counting test points or connectors.

circuits.title: Inverting power supply
circuits.description: The buck converter rearranged to make a negative output from a positive input. The IC's GND pin and the low end of its RT and compensation parts sit on the negative output rail, and the inductor returns to system ground. The catch diode runs from the negative rail up to SW. R1 and R2 divide between system ground and the negative rail onto FB. Cin goes from VIN to system ground and Cd from VIN to the IC ground. EN is left open. No part values are given.

parts.note: polarised input capacitor, VIN to system ground

notes: Application note SLVA317 carries a worked design.

circuits.title: Split-rail power supply with a coupled inductor
circuits.description: A positive and a negative output from one positive input, using a coupled inductor. The primary winding runs from SW to system ground and works as in the inverting supply: the IC ground sits on the negative rail, a Schottky from the negative rail to SW catches the current, and Coneg holds the negative output. The second winding, also returned to ground, charges the positive output through its own Schottky into Copos. The feedback divider spans the positive rail (R1) to FB and the negative rail (R2). EN is left open. No part values are given.

operation.text: Fixed-frequency peak current mode. Each cycle the oscillator turns the high-side switch on, and it turns off when the sensed switch current reaches the level set by COMP. COMP rises and falls with load. Clamping COMP at a maximum gives the current limit; a minimum clamp gives pulse skipping. A compensating ramp added to the sensed current stops sub-harmonic oscillation above 50 % duty without changing the peak current limit.

At light load, once the output is regulated and a cycle ends with its peak switch current under the level that corresponds to roughly 600 mV on COMP, switching stops and COMP is held at 600 mV. The output sags, the loop raises COMP, and switching resumes until COMP falls again. The PLL keeps running, so skipped-mode pulses stay aligned to an external clock. Because the part senses peak current, the load at which skipping starts depends on the inductor; the 3.3 V example enters Eco-mode near 31.4 mA. With no load the input draws 146 µA.

A 0.1 µF X5R or X7R ceramic rated 10 V or more goes from BOOT to SW; the recharge diode is built in. With a small input-to-output difference the switch can stay on at 100 % duty while BOOT-SW stays above 2.1 V. Below that, the switch turns off and a small internal low-side MOSFET pulls SW down to recharge the capacitor. That low-side MOSFET is turned off when the output is above 24 V and back on below 21.5 V. Dropout duty is set mostly by the drops across the switch, the inductor resistance, the catch diode and the board copper.

A transconductance amplifier compares FB with whichever is lower, the soft-start voltage or the 0.8 V reference. Its gm is 350 µA/V in normal running and drops to 78 µA/V during soft-start. The compensation network goes from COMP to ground.

The reference is 0.8 V ±1 % over temperature and supply. A divider from the output to FB sets VOUT; 1 % resistors or better are advised. Larger values raise light-load efficiency but make the loop more sensitive to noise and to the FB input current. Keep at least 1 µA in the divider; the lower resistor should be under 800 kΩ.

The part runs when VIN is above 4.3 V and EN is above 1.2 V, and stops when VIN falls below about 4 V or EN goes below 1.2 V. EN has a 1.2 µA pull-up (I1), so an open pin enables the part. Once EN passes 1.2 V a further 3.4 µA (Ihys) flows out of the pin, and it is removed when EN drops below 1.2 V; with a divider RUVLO1 from VIN to EN and RUVLO2 from EN to ground this sets the start and stop voltages. If the input can rise high enough to push EN over its 8.4 V rating, a zener on EN is advised to clamp it.

The reference is ramped digitally from zero over 1024 switching cycles. Pulling EN below 1.2 V, or a thermal shutdown, resets the soft-start. An overload also resets the soft-start timer, so recovery to the regulated output is ramped.

A resistor from RT/CLK to ground sets 100 kHz to 2500 kHz; the pin sits near 0.5 V and needs that resistor. Higher frequency shrinks the inductor and capacitors, but efficiency, maximum input voltage and the 135 ns minimum on time limit it. The frequency has to stay below both the pulse-skip limit and the foldback limit, and the lower of the two governs.

The peak switch current limit is set by an internal clamp on COMP, with a typical 60 ns delay; smaller inductors let the peak overshoot further during that delay. As FB falls from 0.8 V to 0 V the oscillator frequency is divided by 1, 2, 4 and then 8, lengthening the off time so the inductor current can ramp down during a short. Foldback is digital, so it works while synchronised to an external clock.

A square wave on RT/CLK that goes below 0.5 V and above 1.7 V, with pulses wider than 15 ns, synchronises the part between 160 kHz and 2300 kHz; the SW rising edge follows the clock's falling edge. The clock is AC-coupled through a 10 pF ceramic capacitor. The frequency resistor stays connected from RT/CLK to ground so it takes over when the clock stops; with a low-impedance source, RT goes in series with a termination resistor (for example 50 Ω), the coupling capacitor joining at their junction, and the sum of the two sets the free-running frequency close to the clock. On the first clock edge above the PLL threshold, the 0.5 V source is removed and the PLL locks within 78 µs. When the clock is removed, the frequency drops to 150 kHz before settling at the resistor-set value.

If FB rises above about 109 % of the reference, the high-side switch turns off at once; it resumes when FB falls below about 106 %. This limits overshoot after a fault clears or after a fast load release with little output capacitance.
Switching stops above a junction temperature of 176 °C. Below 164 °C the part starts again through soft-start.

For loop simulation the power stage is a voltage-controlled current source with gmps = 12 A/V feeding the output capacitor and load, and the error amplifier is a 350 µA/V transconductance with an output resistance Ro and capacitance Co setting its open-loop gain and bandwidth. The model holds in continuous conduction only. The power stage has one dominant pole that moves with load, so crossover stays the same as the load changes, plus the output capacitor ESR zero.

Three networks from COMP to ground are supported. Type 2A: a series resistor and capacitor with a second capacitor across them. Type 2B: a series resistor and capacitor alone. Type 1: a single capacitor. The type 2 networks suit low-ESR ceramic output capacitors and high bandwidth; type 1 suits high-ESR aluminium electrolytic or tantalum output capacitors.

Operation is recommended above 4.5 V. The part can run down to its UVLO threshold, typically 4.3 V, and does not switch below it. With EN open or pulled up to VIN, crossing UVLO starts the soft-start sequence.

KIND of up to 0.3 suits low-ESR ceramic output capacitors and 0.2 suits higher-ESR types. Ripple current should always exceed 150 mA for stable PWM, and a wide-input design benefits from fairly large ripple. Because the inductor current can reach the switch current limit in transients, the safest choice is a saturation rating at or above the 5.5 A nominal limit.

Size the output capacitance by the strictest of three limits: holding the output through a load step for about two switching cycles while the loop responds, absorbing the inductor energy on load release (the catch diode cannot sink current), and meeting the ripple specification. In the example the load step governs at 44.9 µF; a 100 µF ceramic with 5 mΩ ESR derates to about 70 µF.

An external diode from SW to ground is required. Its reverse rating should be at least VIN(max), preferably 42 V or more for transients up to the part's rating, and its peak current rating above the maximum inductor current. A Schottky's low forward voltage raises efficiency; at high frequency the junction capacitance adds AC loss. For long periods at light load a diode with lower leakage may be preferred.

At least 3 µF of effective X5R or X7R ceramic capacitance is needed after DC-bias derating, rated above the maximum input voltage and for the input ripple current. Bulk capacitance helps in some designs. If the supply is more than a few inches away, add bulk capacitance, typically a 100 µF electrolytic.

Bypass VIN to ground with a low-ESR X5R or X7R ceramic and keep the loop through that capacitor, VIN and the catch diode anode small. Tie GND straight to the PowerPAD and take the pad to inner ground planes through several vias under the IC. Route SW to the diode cathode and the inductor, with both close to the pin and the SW copper kept small to limit capacitive coupling. At full load the top-side ground area also spreads heat. RT/CLK is noise-sensitive: place the RT resistor close to the IC with short traces. In the example layout the boot capacitor trace runs on another layer so the top-side ground stays wide.
